context: This criteria evaluates correct usage of the library's extensibility API for creating custom math instances and registering new functions. It checks that create() is used to create a custom instance, that import() is used to add new functions, and that the new functions correctly leverage the instance's built-in functions internally.

checklist.name: Uses create() for custom instance
checklist.description: createCustomMath() uses the library's create() function to instantiate a new math instance rather than using the default instance or manually constructing one.

checklist.name: Uses import() to register functions
checklist.description: The new functions (clamp, degToRad, average) are registered on the custom instance using its import() method, making them accessible as first-class methods on the instance.

checklist.name: Functions use instance's built-ins
checklist.description: The custom functions use the math instance's own functions internally (e.g. math.max, math.min, math.pi, math.mean) rather than standalone imports or manual implementations.

checklist.name: Standard functions still available
checklist.description: The returned custom instance retains all standard mathjs functions (e.g. add, sqrt, evaluate still work on the returned instance).

checklist.name: Correct behavior of custom functions
checklist.description: clamp, degToRad, and average all produce correct results: clamp(15, 0, 10) = 10, degToRad(180) ≈ π, average(1,2,3,4,5) = 3.
